problemStatement.plain: For all n ≥ 1, D(n) is the nearest integer to n!/e.
whyMatters: The rounding formula D(n) = round(n!/e) provides a simple computation rule
The unique nearest integer property characterizes D(n) analytically

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: 7 theorems proved, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Fixed DerangementsConvergence.lean syntax and proved the nearest integer theorem.
builtItems: derangements_unique_nearest: D(n) is unique nearest natural to n!/e
insights: Rate scaling: multiply |D(n)/n! - e⁻¹| ≤ 1/(n+1)! by n! to get |D(n) - n!/e| ≤ 1/(n+1)
n=1 case uses Real.add_one_lt_exp one_ne_zero for strict e > 2
Integer gap lemma: omega closes |m-D(n)| < 1 → m = D(n) after Int casting
